President Trump announced a new diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 9 to the surprise of many U.S. allies. Experts argue the agreement could undercut Western economic pressure on Russia and solidarity efforts with Ukraine while doing little to lower fuel prices.

“The announcement of the deal is really for political effect at home, to try to influence voters in this election,” expert Vijay Vaitheeswaran said. “The idea that there might be lower prices coming because of an innovative deal that President Trump did, with his relationship with Putin, sounds pretty good [to voters].”

Beyond lowering fuel prices, the Trump administration reportedly hopes the deal will signal Washington’s openness to working with Moscow and bring the country back to the negotiating table to end the war. Few experts believe the diesel deal will have much of an effect on global oil markets in the near future. Instead, several said it would only bolster Russia economically and further strain transatlantic unity.

“The diesel deal shows that Washington’s Russia policy is now driven by high prices at the pump before the November 3 midterm elections, rather than by any shared transatlantic strategy,” expert @m2matthijs said. “The irony is that the U.S., and especially President Trump, has lectured the Europeans for years about the dangers of buying Russian energy; now it is easing sanctions to buy Russian diesel itself, without consulting anyone in Europe.”

Whether or not it is implemented, the surprise diesel deal has strained relations between the United States and its allies. “For many EU leaders, [the diesel deal] is further proof that the Europeans can no longer afford to outsource their security policy and can no longer rely on the United States to contain Russia,” Matthijs said.

note_tweet.text:
📝 New article on Our World in Data: When do people experience mental health conditions for the first time?

Mental health conditions can begin at almost any age. For many people, they develop in the early stages of life.

Around two-thirds of people who will ever experience a mental health disorder do so by the age of 25.

But this varies a lot by condition.

Some — and in fact the most common mental health disorders — can develop at any point in someone’s life. This includes mood disorders, such as depression and bipolar disorder.

Several are more likely to develop earlier in life, with a very strong peak around adolescence. These include social anxiety, obsessive-compulsive, and eating disorders. Social anxiety, for example, tends to first develop in childhood, and almost 80% of those who will experience it at some point in their lives do so before the age of 18.

Finally, some tend to peak around age 20, but will often still develop later in adulthood. This includes substance use (alcohol and cannabis) disorders and schizophrenia, which commonly develop in someone’s twenties.

Knowing the age at which people might be particularly vulnerable to the onset of a mental health condition is important. It helps societies offer support at the right time to make a difference.

In this article, we look at data on the age of onset of various mental health conditions based on a large meta-analysis of 192 studies.

note_tweet.text:
IT IS BECOMING F*CKING DANGEROUS

A coding agent just improved itself from 20% to 50% on SWE-bench by rewriting its own tools. Not a better model. The code around the model

Darwin Gödel Machine (Sakana AI + UBC). The loop is simple:
> Agent proposes an edit to its own tools and workflow
> Benchmark evaluates the candidate
> Archive keeps the useful branches so the search can jump back

Some weaker versions became ancestors of stronger ones. The gain came from better file-viewing, patch validation, and ranking multiple solutions - the exact things developers normally hardcode by hand

The Chinese labs are already running 300-agent swarms with verification layers. This is the next step: the swarm stops needing a human to redesign the tools every week. The agent starts doing that part itself

20% → 50% in one controlled experiment. The archive is what made the jump possible. Without it, the search only modifies the current winner and gets stuck

The model did not get smarter. The system around it rewrote itself until the tools stopped being the bottleneck

Full roadmap below in this article

Zpráva, že analytici Morgan Stanley snížili odhad poptávky po AI GPU od AMD pro roky 2026 až 2030 o 43,3 % (z asi 14,1 milionů kusů na 8 milionů kusů) při zachování výhledu pro #Nvidia, vyvolala na trzích i na sociálních sítích vcelku rozruch, avšak bez kontextu je to velmi zavádějící. Já jsem se nechal též zmást titulky a musel si report projít.

Ta úprava nepochází od hlavního amerického týmu, který Joseph Moore, který #AMD v USA pokrývá, ale od asijského týmu zaměřeného na dodavatelský řetězec, jehož zjištění se pak využívají u Moora v reportech. 

Ve skutečnosti šlo o korekci dřívějšího extrémně nadhodnoceného modelu asijské divize a jeho sblížení s modely v USA. Zatímco americký tým modeluje dodávky AMD pro roky 2026, 2027 a 2028 na úrovni 672 tisíc kusů, 1,1 milionu a 1,4 milionu kusů, snížený odhad asijského týmu počítá s 600 tisíci, 1,3 milionu a 1,9 milionu kusů. Asijský tým tak i po této revizi zůstává pro roky 2027 a 2028 výrazně optimističtější než ten americký.

Otázka může znít, proč se to tak událo, a proč to nikdo již dříve nekorigoval. Asijské týmy, co jsem obecně zjistil, často modelují objemy přes alokace u třetích stran (TSMC CoWoS, HBM paměti atd.), což v předchozím výhledu vedlo k číslu 14,1 milionů kusů. Snížení na 8 milionů kusů do roku 2030 tak nepředstavuje náhlý propad poptávky, ale spíše očištění od dvojího započítávání v řetězci.

note_tweet.text:
Estoy haciendo algunos pinitos en $IREN y buscando...

La semana pasada $ASML y $TSM noscontaron prácticamente lo mismo, pero cada una desde un eslabón distinto de la cadena de valor.

En la IA ya no se trata tanto de cuánto recurso tienes, sino de cuánto eres capaz de sacar de cada unidad escasa.

Y esto se está viendo en toda la cadena:

$ASML: el precio de sus máquinas va ligado a su productividad. La nueva DUV procesa 330 obleas/hora y la EUV pasa de 230 a 260. Más productividad significa más valor para el cliente y, por tanto, mayor capacidad para subir precios. La máquina es más cara, pero al cliente le sale más rentable.

$TSM: en el Q3 envió apenas un 3% más de obleas, pero facturó un 16% más. Cada oblea le genera ya unos 10.400$, un 13% más que hace solo tres meses. El crecimiento viene de fabricar mejor.

IREN: exactamente la misma lógica, pero aplicada a la energía. Su recurso escaso son los MW. Cuantos más tokens sea capaz de generar por MW, más dólares puede monetizar por cada unidad de energía.

Y aquí entra otro de los grandes protagonistas de este ciclo: la memoria HBM.

ASML está vendiendo más que nunca al segmento de memoria (+75% este año) y TSMC ya advierte de que el encarecimiento de los componentes está empezando a castigar al consumo.

La memoria es cada vez más cara para todos, pero hay un matiz importante.

Si el coste de un servidor sube un 10%, pero su capacidad de generar tokens por MW crece todavía más, el coste por token termina bajando.

Es exactamente lo mismo que ocurre con una máquina de ASML. Pagas más por ella, pero cada oblea te sale más barata.

Y al final de toda esta cadena nos encontramos con el verdadero cuello de botella: la energía.

note_tweet.text:
この記事すごいね
本当に色々衝撃的なことが書いてある
まさかSamsungがTSMCのベースダイをNVHBMとは言え採用する方向とは

サムスン・TSMC、先端プロセス活用しHBM供給量を拡大…「メモリのボトルネック」を突破へ

■サムスン・TSMC「呉越同舟」
独自の「NVHBM」を開発するエヌビディア
「ベースダイ」にTSMCのロジックプロセスを要求
歩留まり90%のファウンドリ技術力を選定
不足する回路部品を補い、製造工程を加速
HBM需要は来年90%増加する見通し
TSMCと手を組み、供給拡大の大きな青写真を描く

サムスン電子（005930）がエヌビディア向けのカスタム広帯域メモリ（HBM）の開発過程において、ファウンドリ（半導体受託生産）の競合であるTSMCと手を組むことになったのは、人工知能（AI）チップが性能と供給の両面で「メモリのボトルネック」に直面しているためだ。HBMのデータ転送速度が画像処理装置（GPU）の演算速度に追いつかないという技術的な壁が浮上するなか、TSMCの先端ロジック（システム半導体）プロセスによってHBMの性能を引き上げ、さらにTSMCの生産能力を加えて供給を増やすという構想を後押しした形だ。

18日の業界関係者によると、エヌビディアはサムスン電子・TSMCと共に、独自HBMである「NVHBM」の中核部品「ベースダイ」をカスタム設計している。HBMの最下層に位置するベースダイはロジック回路で構成されており、データ転送速度を決定づける。これをいかに設計するかによって製品の競争力が左右される。

NVHBM向けのカスタムベースダイは、従来GPU側にあったメモリコントローラーを実装している点が特徴だ。GPUが担っていた付随機能をNVHBMのベースダイに移管し、その分確保されたGPUのスペースに演算回路をさらに詰め込むことで性能を引き上げた。その代わり、ベースダイにコントローラーを収めるスペースを確保するため、外部チップと電気信号を送受信する回路である物理層（PHY）の面積を標準的なHBMより60%縮小した。その結果、NVHBMは標準のHBM4E（第7世代）に比べ、メモリ帯域幅を最大30%拡大し、消費電力を15%削減できるようになった。

エヌビディアがNVHBM用のベースダイにTSMCの3nm（ナノメートル・10億分の1メートル）ロジックプロセスを要求したのは、こうした設計方式と密接に関係している。ベースダイにGPUから移した機能まで盛り込むには、限られた面積により多くの回路を集積できる3ナノ級の超微細プロセスが不可欠だ。さらに生産コストを抑えるためには、歩留まり（ウェハー1枚あたりの良品チップの割合）も高くなければならない。

業界では、TSMCの3ナノプロセスの歩留まりを90%以上、これに対応するサムスンファウンドリの2ナノ（SF2）プロセスを60%前後とみている。エヌビディアとしては、ベースダイの工程をTSMCに一本化することが安定した選択肢となるわけだ。

技術的な条件や環境以上に大きな理由は、HBMの供給が需要に追いついていない点にある。投資銀行UBSによると、来年のHBM需要はビット（記憶容量の単位）基準で約615億Gb（ギガビット）に達し、今年より91%増加すると予測されている。一方、メモリメーカー各社の新規出荷量は546億Gbにとどまると予想されており、需要に対して10%ほどの供給不足が懸念されている状況だ。

サムスン電子は急増する需要に合わせ、HBMの2大中核部品である「コアダイ」と「ベースダイ」の生産量を同時に増やさなければならない。メモリ半導体の役割を果たすコアダイは、先端DRAMプロセスである「1c（第6世代）」を活用し、華城（ファソン）キャンパスの17ラインおよび平沢（ピョンテク）キャンパスのP2・P3・P4で製造している。さらに、再来年の初稼働を目指して建設中のP5-1も、1cラインを中心に運営される予定だ。

しかし、ベースダイの生産能力は相対的に限られている。サムスン電子の4ナノ・ベースダイ生産ラインは、華城17ラインと平沢P3の一部にしかない。既存のHBM需要に合わせて組まれた現行の生産体制では、NVHBMのようなカスタムHBMの物量まで十分に消化するのは難しい状況だ。

サムスン電子がカバーしきれないベースダイの不足分は、TSMCが補える余力を持っている。これに先立ちTSMCは第3四半期の決算発表で、台湾・台南の「Fab 18」に新規の3ナノ生産ラインを2カ所追加し、それぞれ来年上半期と再来年上半期から量産に入ると明らかにした。米アリゾナ第2工場と日本の熊本第2工場でも、それぞれ来年第3四半期と2028年の量産を目標に3ナノ生産ラインを備える計画だ。

かといって、ベースダイの生産がTSMCに完全に固定されたわけではない。サムスン電子はエヌビディアの要求に従ってNVHBMにTSMC製のベースダイを採用しつつも、持続的な需要増加に備えて自社ファウンドリで生産する 방안（方策）も準備している。

業界関係者は「TSMCの3ナノ生産ラインはベースダイ以外にも高性能コンピューティング（HPC）やスマートフォン向けチップを製造しており、割り当てられる生産量に限界が来る可能性がある」とし、「そのためサムスンファウンドリは、TSMCの3ナノに準ずるサムスンの2ナノプロセスでNVHBMベースダイの生産検証を進めている」と語った。

また別の業界専門家は「エヌビディアのNVHBM共同開発を機に、サムスン電子とTSMCの協力関係が先端パッケージング工程からHBMの中核部品を製造する関係へと広がった」とし、「4年前にTSMCのAIチップパッケージング工程（CoWoS）関連で協力した実績のある両社が、世界的な『メモリ不足（メモリ・쇼티지）』の局面で再び手を組んだことは、業界に大きな示唆を与えている」と評価した。

https://t.co/UdlQkEw2g6

note_tweet.text:
Quantum FUD has gotten quieter, but math keeps moving. Quick update on quantum vs bitcoin:

The estimated "logical qubit" requirements for attacking Bitcoin's secp256k1 have fallen from ~2,300 to Google's 1,175, and now below 900 in the latest https://t.co/k03v97LCbQ work by Jieyi Long (Theta Labs).

A lot of that progress happened in 2026, with AI helping optimize the algorithmic circuits.

But what about the actual hardware?

IonQ recently estimated that breaking a Bitcoin private key would require ~20,000 "physical qubits" (note there is a diff between physical and logical) and would take 26 days.

Interestingly, IonQ's own roadmap targets 20,000 physical qubits and 1,600 logical qubits by 2028. 

Just TWO YEARS away.

Let's compare that to everyone else:

IonQ:
2024 - 36+ physical qubits
2025 - 64-100+
2026 - 100-256+ (target)
2027 - 10,000 (target!)
2028 - 20,000 (target!)

IBM:
2025 - 120 physical qubits on Nighthawk
2029 - 200 logical qubits (target)
2033+ - 2,000 logical qubits (target)

Google:
2024 - 105 physical qubits on Willow
2026 - Still working toward large-scale fault tolerance, with no comparable public deadline for thousands of logical qubits.

IonQ has actually hit several past performance milestones early, but going from a few hundred physical qubits to 10,000 in a single year is an entirely different challenge.

And physical qubit counts alone don't tell the story. Error correction, gate fidelity, connectivity and runtime matter enormously. These companies also use different architectures, so the numbers aren't directly interchangeable.

IonQ's 2028 projection is incredibly aggressive compared to IBM and Google. 

Could they pull it off? 

Maybe... but I wouldn't confuse a corporate roadmap with a working quantum computer capable of breaking Bitcoin.

The algorithms are getting cheaper fast. 
The hardware remains the big question and ultimate limiter (still after 20 years) of quantum computing.

I don't think Bitcoin is about to be broken, but I also think the community could start to prepare now...

note_tweet.text:
A QUANTUM COMPUTER JUST BEAT GOOGLE’S ERROR RECORD BY 100X

$QNT (Quantinuum), reported this morning that its Helios machine hit 99.9995% logical fidelity. In plain terms, a protected qubit now makes about five errors per million operations. A month ago the same hardware held the record at roughly fifty.

A quantum computer is useless until its errors are rare enough to correct faster than they appear. Every roadmap to a useful machine is really a roadmap to that error rate. Quantinuum says it’s now inside the range its 2029 fault tolerant machine Apollo, was designed around.

They compared it to about 100 times fewer errors than the best published result on Google’s superconducting chips. Trapped ions are slower than superconductors, but each operation is far cleaner, and today that gap got wider.

The new code uses up to 37 physical qubits to make one good logical qubit, up from 10 in September. Better qubits, bought with more of them. The number comes from a company release, not yet a peer-reviewed paper. A Sandia physicist not involved in the work said it could mean useful fault tolerance at under a million physical qubits.

Google cut magic state errors 40x last Wednesday. Quantinuum cut logical errors 10x today. The physics is moving faster than the stocks.

note_tweet.text:
NYT: "Surging exports and the industrial production needed to sustain them kept China’s economy growing over the past three months, even as consumer spending stagnated and investment plunged. The result is an economy increasingly dependent on selling goods abroad, even as domestic demand deteriorates."

NYT's Keith Bradsher gets this right. Many other analysts have been presenting this year's economic data as describing a two-track economy, with a sluggish domestic economy being balanced by a brilliant export economy.

But that is a very poor description of what is actually happening. Yes, net exports are surging, but this isn't a sign of a viable export sector. If the export sector were very profitable, it might make sense to describe it this way, but exports aren't especially profitable except in relation to domestic sales, where except in a few sectors businesses are struggling to make any profit at all, and once direct and indirect subsidies are backed out, much of China's exports are net value destroyers for the economy, with the losses capitalized on balance sheets in the form of surging debt.

When an economy produces far more than it can absorb through domestic consumption or investment, it must either export the balance or close down domestic production. Given how high real unemployment is, especially among the young, Beijing has no choice but to force the former, even if this comes at an economic cost.

The surge in China's net exports, in other words, is not a sigh of a strong and profitable export sector. If it takes rising debt, continued subsidies, and growing exports in order to prevent a contraction in domestic production, the surge in net exports is simply another way of describing weak domestic demand.

Surging exports are usually a good sign for an economy. Surging net exports usually are not.
https://t.co/yWXprpdixG

None of the data that came out today gives us a different picture of the Chinese economy from what we’ve seen all year. The economy is still heavily focused on boosting production and is still struggling with boosting demand. 

GDP grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter of 2026, slightly higher than expected, from 5.0% in the first quarter and 4.3% in the second quarter. Year to date GDP has grown 4.6%, just above the bottom of the GDP growth target for 2026.

In September, industrial output went up by 5.5% year on year, or 5.3% for the first nine months. Meanwhile retail sales increased by 1.1% in September, or 2.6% for the first nine months.

The gap between domestic production and domestic consumption, in other words, continues to widen rather than narrow, with the gap much wider in September than it has been over the rest of the year. This can only be balanced by rising investment or a rising trade surplus.

And it clearly isn’t being balanced by rising investment. Fixed asset investment in the first nine months of 2026 was down 7.2% year on year, or 4.2% with property investment deducted.

The decline in overall investment was driven by an even sharper decline in private investment, which was down by 10.4% year on year, or 6.7% with property investment deducted. Disaggregated by sector, investment in infrastructure declined by 4.2% year on year, manufacturing by 2.1%, and real estate development by 20.6%. The good news is that the decline in investment may finally be bottoming out, with fixed asset investment in September, rising by 0.07% month on month.

We will probably see fiscal expansion in the last quarter of this year, although I think it would be a good thing if Beijing let growth come in at the bottom of the target, especially if they lower the target further in 2027. Debt is simply growing too fast, and it is growing fast only because of the urgent desire to meet politically-determined GDP growth targets. The longer this goes on, the more difficult the ultimate adjustment will be.

urls.description: Large language models increasingly write the code behind empirical research. This column reports a benchmark of 40 econometric tasks in Stata, R, and Python. For each task, two leading models write a script, as a chatbot that never runs it and as an agent that runs and revises it. Letting the models run their code raises the share of correct results from 79% to 97% and makes the prompt and the software matter far less. The failures that remain under the agent come from scripts that run without errors but return wrong numbers, and detecting them is still the researcher’s work.
urls.title: Letting AI agents write econometric code

My coworker's mother passed away last November.

She left her modest $190,000 house to him clear and free, no mortgage, completely paid off after thirty years of factory work.

He moved into the home in January to finally settle the estate.

Two weeks ago, a letter arrived from the state Medicaid estate recovery office.

Because his mother spent four months in a rehabilitation facility before she passed, the state quietly slapped a retroactive $114,000 lien against the property title.

He called the state health department, frantic, asking how a hospital stay could bankrupt an inherited home that had no mortgage balance.

The caseworker sighed and told him:

"Federal law requires state programs to claw back healthcare costs from deceased estates. The house cannot be sold or transferred until the balance is cleared in full."

He offered to pay a monthly settlement.

They said no. The full $114,000 is due in 60 days, or they foreclose on the property at a public auction.

A lifetime of working-class savings, wiped out overnight by a retroactive healthcare lien.

You don't own generational wealth.

You're just holding a property title until the state finds a legal mechanism to repossess it the moment you die.

Understanding IREN isnt that hard.

For IREN, HBM improving efficiency has at least three layers.

First is the customer math.
More HBM capacity, higher memory bandwidth, can run a bigger model.
What the customer cares about is how many more tokens they get for the same hour of money.

Second is pricing power.
Who has the lower total cost for the same job.
Comparing $NBIS, $IREN, and $CRWV on hourly rent alone isnt enough.
Look at price divided by effective token throughput.

Third is the one I watch. Revenue per MW.
Every data center is capped by power.
That flows through.
More tokens per MW
→ higher customer value
→ higher dollars per MW
→ shorter payback.

IREN recent 3-year contracts are already above $20M per MW a year. Company puts payback at about 2 years.

So the way I read it now, whats scarce is how many useful tokens a MW can keep producing.

$MU moving, HBM getting more expensive, does lift IRENs server cost.

If the server goes from 100 to 110, and the new HBM lifts token throughput by more than that, the customers cost per token can still come down.

Thats what Im hoping for.

Then IREN has a shot at higher utilization, pricing power, and better revenue per MW at the same time.

note_tweet.text:
GOOGLE IS ONE STEP CLOSER TO A FAULT TOLERANT QUANTUM COMPUTER 

Every useful quantum computer needs a supply of something called magic states. They’re the ingredient that lets a machine run real algorithms instead of simple ones, they can’t be reused, and making them is so expensive that some estimates say 95% of a future quantum computer’s capacity would go to manufacturing them. That’s been the quiet bottleneck behind every roadmap in the industry.

Today Google published a paper in Science showing a new way to make them on its Willow chip. Instead of building a magic state from scratch at huge cost, you start with a rough one, grow it inside a small protected patch of the chip, measure it over and over, throw away every attempt that shows an error, and keep the survivors. They call it cultivation.

The numbers were a 40-fold cut in errors versus the raw state, and the highest-fidelity magic state ever produced on hardware, 99.99%. They also showed the grown state can be transplanted from one type of error correcting code into another, which is the plumbing a real machine needs.

Google’s own caveat is that it has to work at much larger scale before it counts for practical computing. Fair, but the bottleneck everyone assumed would be the expensive part just got a lot cheaper, on a chip that exists.

Ben Horowitz says Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies he’s ever seen on security

"The irony on these things is wild. Anthropic is one of the most negligent companies that we've ever seen in terms of their own security."

"They let Claude code, one of their crown jewels, just like walk out the door because they had such bad OPSEC."

"I'll tell you a funny story. So when we first got Opus 4.5, we were doing cybersecurity checks for the firm. So we had an agent basically set up a website for a pet store. And then we took another agent and said, 'Tell us if we can exploit that web store.' And it gave us all the exploits it could find. So Opus 4.5 wrote really buggy code. Great."

"And then we said, 'Oh, the SQL injection you found, is that actually exploitable?' And it goes, 'Let's pop it open.' And the agent using Opus 4.5 breaks into the website and steals all the [data], and we call Anthropic. And what they tell us is, 'You prompted it wrong.' That was their answer."

"So these guys are doing that on the one hand. And then on the other hand, they're coming up with theoretical scenarios about other people's software. That's bad. And so like, what the hell."

"On the distillation thing, you know, to build their model, they distilled the works of every author, every creative, every scientist for the last 2000 years. For them to be complaining about distillation, which, by the way, distilling a model is not even illegal. It's just a violation of the terms of service." 

"It's just so much. And the fact that they get people to write things supporting these bananas, ridiculous, two-faced ideas. And the timing here is very suspicious."
